name: Bani
overview: Bani was a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the son of Shemer. He belonged to the Levitical family associated with the Merarites, descendants of Merari, son of Levi, through Mushi. His lineage places him within the priestly and service-oriented tribe set apart for duties related to the tabernacle.
namesAndTitles: The name Bani is a proper name meaning 'descendant.' There is no indication that this name was given directly by God. It reflects a common Hebrew personal name without additional titles or meanings noted in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Bani was the son of Shemer. It is also inferred that Amzi was his father, establishing his place within the Levitical genealogy. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are detailed.
scriptureSignificance: Bani's significance lies in his role within the Levitical lineage, specifically among the Merarites, who were responsible for particular aspects of tabernacle service. His genealogy helps trace the organization and duties of the Levites, emphasizing the continuity of God's appointed servants. Though not a prominent figure in narrative events, Bani represents the faithful descendants entrusted with sacred responsibilities.
